accuracy_on_these_frames.threshold_source: selected on the neurips2020 val split, held fixed

caveats: Two AC backends give two different ratios. LightSim generated every dataset in data/ and is the honest headline; PandaPower is the reference implementation and yields a ~10x larger ratio. Never quote one without naming which.
Snapshot sets differ between backend runs: same seed and same do-nothing policy, but not bit-identical trajectories. Comparisons are exact WITHIN an artifact and indicative across two.
obs.simulate is a pipeline, not a raw solver — it includes grid2op action construction and observation building, and it solves the t+1 forecast injections rather than the current instant.
The GNN was timed on every available device; AC is CPU-bound and single-threaded. Quote the CPU row whenever an accelerator row is quoted, or the comparison confounds 'GNN vs AC' with 'GPU vs CPU'.
Timing is hardware-dependent. The ratio is the result; the absolute seconds describe the one machine recorded in `environment`.
The GNN batches; AC is serial by construction. That is a real architectural advantage, which is why batch-1 latency is reported beside it.
Batch size 64 is load-bearing: BatchNorm(track_running_stats=False) uses live batch statistics, so the accuracy figures here hold at 64 only. Never mix them with figures taken at another batch size.
The speed buys a measured accuracy loss. AC is ground truth (F1 1.0); the GNN scores 0.8956 / 0.4167 / 0.5577 at the held threshold, and on case14 it loses to answering 'violation' every time.
